claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning a formal assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me help you through this. 

To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask you about your child or children.

**First, I need to know about the child(ren) you're claiming for:**

1. **How old is your child?** (Or if you have multiple children, what are their ages?)

This will help me understand which rules apply to your situation. Child Benefit has different requirements depending on whether the child is:
- **Under 16 years old** (generally automatic eligibility if other conditions are met)
- **16-19 years old** (eligibility depends on whether they're in education or training)
- **20 years or older** (generally not eligible)

Please share the age(s) of the child or children you're inquiring about.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 5 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you're asking about **Alex, who is 5 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, that's great news - he falls into the category where Child Benefit eligibility is more straightforward. Now I need to check a few other important conditions.

Let me move forward with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

For a 5-year-old, this is typically not applicable, so the answer should be straightforward - children this age wouldn't normally be in paid work. But I need to confirm: **Is Alex in any paid work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 5! He's not working at all.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That makes perfect sense. Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?**

Specifically, is he not receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit (in his own right)

At age 5, this is also unlikely, but I need to confirm: **Is Alex receiving any of these benefits in his own name?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just 5!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

At 5 years old, this is very unlikely! I just need to confirm: **Is Alex currently in any type of apprenticeship (whether in England, Scotland, or Wales)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not - he's only 5 years old! He's not in any apprenticeship.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me move forward:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now I need to check your residency situation. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.**

There are several ways you could qualify on residency grounds. Let me ask you some key questions:

**1. Do you normally live in the UK?** (This is the most straightforward path)

If not, I can also check alternative eligibility routes, such as:
- Having settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Various pre-settled status scenarios
- Crown servant living abroad
- Other special circumstances

Please start by telling me: **Do you normally live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's perfect. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Are you responsible for Alex?**

The rules define responsibility in several ways. Let me check which applies to you:

**Do you:**
1. **Live with Alex?** (This is the most straightforward path)

Or if not:
2. Are you **contributing to his upkeep** (e.g., paying for his food, clothes, housing, pocket money, presents)?
3. Are you **paying maintenance** under a court order or agreement?

Which of these applies to your situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Important question: Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent claiming Child Benefit for him?
- Is another family member claiming Child Benefit for him?

Or are you the only person claiming for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex - it's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Where is Alex currently living?**

Does any of the following apply:
1. **Is Alex in hospital?**
2. **Is Alex in residential care** (e.g., a care home)?
3. **Is Alex being fostered?**
4. **Is Alex living normally at home with you?**

Which applies to Alex's situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living normally at home with me - none of those special situations apply.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Final question: Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the council paying for any part of Alex's care or housing? Or are you responsible for all of his upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything - I'm responsible for all of his care and upkeep myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's wonderful news. Let me proceed to the final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! 🎉

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ You Are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit

**Summary for Alex:**

You meet all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit. Here's why:

✓ **Age:** Alex is 5 years old (qualifying child under 16)  
✓ **Residency:** You live in the UK (Manchester)  
✓ **Responsibility:** You live with Alex and are responsible for his care and upkeep  
✓ **No disqualifying factors:** Alex isn't working, receiving benefits in his own right, in an apprenticeship, in special accommodation, or the subject of another claim  
✓ **Council support:** The council isn't paying towards his accommodation or maintenance

### Next Steps - How to Claim:

1. **Apply online** at [www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim) or **by post** using form CH2
2. **Gather required documents:**
   - Proof of your identity
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
   - Proof of your residency (e.g., utility bill, council tax letter)

3. **Important to note:** If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may be subject to the **High Income Child Benefit Charge**, which means you may need to repay some or all of the benefit through self-assessment.

4. **Payment:** Child Benefit is usually paid every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain other benefits).

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit, or do you have any other children you'd like me to check eligibility for?

Alex meets all Child Benefit eligibility requirements.
